label: Gas flames: did a hot flame light
definition: A gas fuel burned from a spherical burner into a chamber atmosphere. 'A hot flame lit' = PSI's 'Hot ignition: yes'. Inverse-flame tests are left out: their oxygen is the burner stream, not the chamber. Brief flashes are counted but not modelled.

skill.gate: Estimates are shown only if cross-validated accuracy beats always guessing the commoner outcome by 5% and AUC is at least 0.70.
skill.reason: Accuracy 74% against 74% for always guessing the commoner outcome, AUC 0.54: the model does not beat guessing by enough, so only observed counts are shown.

patterns.text: At 0.40 oxygen or more, the outcome was "a hot flame lit" in all 12 tests and "no hot flame" in none.
20 of 179 usable tests lie inside the selected habitat's oxygen and pressure box; the outcome was "a hot flame lit" in 17 of them.
